title: 教育回报、收入差距与父母教养方式选择
authors: 吴贾, 刘亚淇, 黄子彬, 楚鹏飞
abstract: 本文分析了我国权威型教养方式背后的社会经济动因,其与社会教育回报率和地区收入差距有直接联系。本文利用2005年人口抽样调查和多项微观调查数据,研究发现父母在26-40岁经历的教育回报率每提高1个百分点,其采取权威型教养方式的概率将提高1.21个百分点。地区收入差距会进一步扩大教育回报率对教养方式选择的影响,因为在收入差距越大的地区,父母越有动力严格要求子女,提高其教育水平,从而实现社会经济地位向上流动。机制分析表明,高教育回报率会增强父母对教育价值的认同和对子女的学历期望。本文还分析了权威型教养方式的积极影响及其可能产生的成本。本研究为理解家庭养育中的“内卷”行为提供了经济学解释。

title: Losses from a Disability: Temporal Variety and Earnings in the Long Run
authors: Daniel S. Hamermesh
official: 官方在线 2026-07-02 · 来源：出版社网页
abstract: Using diaries covering 25-61-year-olds in the American Time Use Survey 2009-24, this study demonstrates that temporal variety—doing more different things in a day—is income superior. Linking these data to underlying Current Population Surveys, propensity-score models show that people stating that they have a mobility/physical disability in each of two consecutive annual surveys undertake almost 4 percent fewer activities per day than other, demographically identical individuals. They also earn about 50 percent less. Combining the estimated impact of income on temporal variety with the implied reductions in variety incurred by those with the disability yields a monetary equivalent of lost variety exceeding that of lost earnings. Measuring disability status only once yields much smaller estimated shortfalls in temporal variety and earnings. That suggests that one-time self-reports of disabilities, which underlie the bulk of studies on the impacts of disabilities on earnings, also underestimate long-term effects.

title: The Economics of Marriage Payments: Bride Price, Dowry, and Dower
title_zh: 婚姻支付的经济学：聘礼、嫁妆与寡妇产
authors: Siwan Anderson
official: 官方在线 2026-06-30 · 来源：出版社网页
abstract: Marriage payments are transfers made in connection with marriage and are among the most widespread and enduring institutions in human history. They can be categorized into three forms: bride price, paid by the groom or his family to the bride’s parents; dowry, transferred from the bride’s family to the groom or his kin; and dower, paid by the groom directly to the bride and retained as her property. Although their prevalence has declined in many industrialized societies, marriage payments remain common across large parts of Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Oceania. Their persistence reflects the fact that they serve multiple economic and social functions simultaneously. Marriage payments can facilitate matching in marriage markets, redistribute marital surplus, transfer wealth across generations, provide insurance within marriage, and signal status, prestige, and adherence to social norms. Marriage payments influence a wide range of outcomes, including household savings, fertility decisions, child marriage, educational investments, migration, bargaining power within marriage, and marital stability. Their effects often extend beyond the married couple themselves, shaping intergenerational patterns of wealth transmission and human capital formation. As such, the consequences of marriage payments are far-reaching. Their welfare implications depend critically on the direction of transfers, who retains control over them after marriage, and the broader legal and social institutions in which they are embedded. In some settings, marital transfers can enhance women’s economic security and bargaining power. In others, they may contribute to gender inequality, violence, coercion, son preference, and constraints on women’s autonomy. The significance of these welfare consequences warrants the attention of policymakers. Accordingly, marriage payments have generated considerable debate and ongoing efforts toward legal reform. At the same time, the diversity of marriage payment systems suggests caution in the design of public policy. Blanket prohibitions or externally imposed reforms may overlook the multiple functions these institutions perform and may generate unintended consequences. More promising approaches may focus on mitigating specific harmful features while preserving functions that families value, particularly where marriage payments remain deeply embedded in local social, economic, and legal systems.
abstract_zh: 婚姻支付是与婚姻相关的财产转移，是人类历史上最普遍且最持久的制度之一。其形式可分为三类：聘礼，由新郎或其家庭支付给新娘父母；嫁妆，从新娘家庭转移给新郎或其亲属；以及聘金，由新郎直接支付给新娘并作为其个人财产保留。尽管在众多工业化社会中婚姻支付的盛行程度有所下降，但在亚洲、非洲、中东和大洋洲的大部分地区，婚姻支付仍然普遍存在。其持续性反映了这些支付同时服务于多种经济和社会功能。婚姻支付可以促进婚姻市场中的匹配、重新分配婚姻剩余、实现代际财富转移、在婚姻内部提供保险，并传递地位、声望及对社会规范的遵从。婚姻支付影响广泛的结果，包括家庭储蓄、生育决策、童婚、教育投资、迁移、婚姻内部议价能力以及婚姻稳定性。其影响往往超越夫妻本身，塑造代际财富传递模式和人力资本形成。因此，婚姻支付的后果具有深远影响。其福利效应关键取决于转移的方向、婚后谁保留对转移财产的控制权，以及这些支付所嵌入的更广泛的法律和社会制度。在某些情境下，婚姻转移可以增强女性的经济安全和议价能力；在其他情境下，则可能加剧性别不平等、暴力、胁迫、男孩偏好以及对女性自主权的限制。这些福利后果的重要性值得政策制定者关注。相应地，婚姻支付引发了大量争论和持续的法律改革努力。同时，婚姻支付体系的多样性提示公共政策设计需谨慎。全面禁止或外部强加的改革可能忽视这些制度所履行的多重功能，并可能产生意外后果。更有前景的方法可能是聚焦于减轻特定有害特征，同时保留家庭所珍视的功能，尤其是在婚姻支付仍深深嵌入当地社会、经济和法律体系的地区。

title: Eco‐Industrial Parks, Green Innovation and Green Export Performance: Evidence From China
title_zh: 生态工业园区、绿色创新与绿色出口绩效：来自中国的证据
authors: Cui Hongxia, Yang Gaoju, Pu Long
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how Eco‐industrial Parks (EIPs) in China shape firm green innovation and, furthermore, explores its implications for trade competitiveness. We find that EIPs significantly boost green patent applications, particularly substantive innovations. This effect is stronger in cleaner industries, environmentally stringent cities and firms with high media exposure. Mechanisms include eased financing constraints, and increased R&D investment. Extending the analysis to the trade domain, we further show that EIP‐induced green innovation enhances firms' performance in green exports. Thus, EIPs serve as a pivotal policy that fosters green innovation and cultivates competitive advantages in global green markets.

title: Consequences of land retirement policies on agricultural labor and land tenure: Evidence from the historical Conservation Reserve Program in the United States
title_zh: 土地休耕政策对农业劳动力和土地保有权的影响：来自美国历史性保护储备计划的证据
authors: Aparna Howlader, Liqing Li
abstract: Abstract Voluntary agricultural land retirement programs are widely recognized for their environmental benefits, yet their economic effects, particularly on labor markets and land tenure, remain less understood. This paper examines the short‐ and long‐term impacts of the first large‐scale US land retirement initiative, the historical Conservation Reserve Program, introduced under the 1956 Set‐Aside Act. Between 1957 and 1960, the program enrolled more than 30 million acres under 3‐, 5‐, or 10‐year contracts, which then expired gradually through 1970. Using a newly digitized Conservation Reserve Program enrollment database linked to agricultural census data from the 1950s through the 1970s, we find that counties with medium and high enrollment intensity experienced statistically significant declines in tenant‐cultivated land relative to low‐enrollment counties during the program's active years. In medium‐enrollment counties, tenant‐operated land declined by roughly 0.6 percentage points, while high‐enrollment counties experienced declines of approximately 1.6 percentage points nationally. The proportion of tenant farm operators also fell in both medium‐ and high‐enrollment counties. These effects were larger and more persistent in the South, especially in counties with higher shares of nonwhite farm operators and sharecropping.

title: Regularization of Synthetic Controls for Policy Evaluation
title_zh: 政策评估中合成控制法的正则化
authors: Yi‐Ting Chen
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a unified framework for interpreting and comparing a broad class of synthetic control (SC) methods. Our framework is built on an analysis of a mean‐squared prediction error (MSPE) bound for the counterfactual predicted by a generic SC method, without imposing a specific outcome model. Using this framework, we develop a generalized SC method that provides a more comprehensive regularization of the MSPE bound than several existing SC methods. Through simulation studies and placebo analyses, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in predicting the counterfactual.

title: Firm Responses to Hiring and Investment Subsidies: Regression Discontinuity Evidence from the California Competes Tax Credit
title_zh: 企业应对招聘与投资补贴的反应：来自加州竞争税收抵免的断点回归证据
authors: Benjamin Hyman, Matthew Freedman, Shantanu Khanna, David Neumark
abstract: Abstract We examine firm responses to state hiring and investment subsidies. We leverage institutional features of the California Competes Tax Credit (CCTC), a large-scale business incentive program that incorporates best practices from prior job creation policies. The CCTC award selection procedure combines formula-based and discretionary components. Leveraging applicant score eligibility cutoffs in a regression discontinuity design and taking advantage of rich longitudinal microdata on establishments and their parent firms, we find that businesses expand employment in California in response to CCTC awards. There is little evidence that these expansions come at the expense of firms’ operations in other states. Our results suggest that targeted and audited hiring and investment subsidies can be effective in promoting local business expansions without inducing significant cross-state displacement effects.
